result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. The reviewer's second pass reported no findings.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model outputs a request and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | You chose "it will eventually fix the bug". Repeating a failing step won't succeed, so the program needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | 4 is right, but "the model runs one tool itself each time" is wrong. The model only requests, and the program runs the tool and calls the model again. |
| q5 | correct | Both parts: the result goes back as the next input, so the model can decide its next step. |
| q6 | partial | "By the name" is only part of it. The model also sees each tool's description and parameters. |

**You have down:** the loop, and that tool results feed the next model call.

**Work on next:** that the program, not the model, runs tools (q4), and that every loop needs a stopping condition (q3).

**Reread before trying again:**
- "The tool-use contract" in [How tool use works](https://platform.claude.com/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/how-tool-use-works).
- The "Agents" part of "Building blocks, workflows, and agents" in [Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents).
- "Specifying client tools" in [Define tools](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/define-tools).

The workspace had no lessons or cheat sheets, so I took the pointers from those web sources and added them to `RESOURCES.md`. I also wrote `learning-records/0003-who-runs-tools-and-stopping.md`, updated `NOTES.md`, and saved the review record in `review-records/`. `submissions/s1.json` is still ungraded; do you want me to grade it too?
